findings.note: A capability entry is appended only after all of its trigger and conditional-facet evaluations finish. If a dependency fails midway through that capability, evaluations already performed for it disappear from the Resolver Evidence, contrary to REQ-004's requirement to record every evaluation actually performed. The failure-after-WARN fixture only fails in a later capability and does not cover this partial-current-capability case.

The three evaluation-abort handlers deliberately discard warn_diagnostics already encountered. This conflicts with REQ-004's requirement that diagnostics record every diagnostic-worthy condition encountered, not only the fatal condition; the implementation avoids a warn-only diagnostic ID by omitting known WARNs entirely.

The verification contract retains a stale claim that the current staged resolver hash is f6bc6796..., while the bundled MANIFEST and declared output identify aaf23df2.... Later report text supersedes other historical values, but the contract's own current-hash statement remains internally inconsistent.
